name: Ndebele Painted Houses
summary: A distinctive architectural style featuring brightly painted geometric patterns on house walls by the Ndebele people.
description: Characterized by bold geometric designs in vibrant colors covering the entire exterior surfaces of buildings. Evolved from traditional Ndebele cultural practices as a form of identity expression and resistance during colonial times.
culturalContext: Southern Ndebele women of South Africa transformed colonial contact into paint: after forced settlement and the 1883 defeat, women began painting homestead walls in bold geometric patterns — Samuels-style diagonal lines, corner chevrons, later wheel and airplane motifs borrowed from passing modernity — using earth pigments then acrylics. The art is matrilineal (mothers train daughters), seasonal (redone after rains), and internationally recognized through Esther Mahlangu's BMW Art Car (1991) and gallery murals.
